draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Yelagiri! The road up here climbs 14 hairpin bends, each named after a Tamil poet, like Pari Valaivu and Kamban Valaivu, and at the top the hills hold 14 small tribal hamlets.
draft.hungryLine: Look out for jackfruit, it's everywhere in summer and the fruit here is considered very good, plus guava and custard apple in season.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Climb Swami Malai, the highest peak, about an hour up from the hamlet of Mangalam. If you're up for more, Jalagamparai Waterfalls is a tough 5 km trek downhill.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Stop at the little observatory after the 12th hairpin bend and look out over the plains through its telescope.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Near the Swami Malai trekking spot, fruit sellers often surprise you by giving more than you paid for.

spots.name: Swami Malai
spots.detail: Starts from Mangalam · The highest peak, an easy hour's climb

spots.name: Jalagamparai Waterfalls
spots.detail: 5 km trek downhill · Big valley views and a temple next to the falls

status.text: Often dry in winter and April to May

spots.name: Don Bosco Centre
spots.detail: Yelagiri Hills · Founded by Fr. Guezou from France, teaching IT to local youth

tips.title: Trek early.
tips.body: Start your climbs at dawn and be back before 9AM, because once the sun is up it gets uncomfortable fast.

tips.title: Don't feed the animals.
tips.body: You'll see monkeys, oxen and goats on the way up, but they can be dangerous, so keep your snacks to yourself.

story.title: Hill villages
story.body: Yelagiri is made up of 14 hamlets in the Eastern Ghats. The tribal families here farm, grow fruit and work the forests, and their unique houses draw visitors.

story.title: The poets' road
story.body: The 14 hairpin bends up the hill were each named after a Tamil poet. A small observatory after the 12th bend points a telescope at the plains.

story.title: Year-round hill station
story.body: With a pleasant climate all year, winters don't keep visitors away. The Don Bosco Centre, started by Fr. Guezou from France, trains local youth in IT.
